note_text:
CC: 62-year-old woman referred by urology for evaluation of urinary incontinence and voiding difficulty.

HPI: Patient reports several months of urinary urgency, urge incontinence episodes 2-3 times per week, and a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying. She denies dysuria or hematuria. No fevers or flank pain. She has tried timed voiding and pelvic floor exercises without significant improvement.

PMH: Hypertension, two prior vaginal deliveries.

Exam: Abdomen soft, nontender, no suprapubic fullness. Pelvic exam reveals grade 2 cystocele on straining; no other significant descensus noted. Neurologic exam of lower extremities is normal.

UA/microscopy: Clean-catch specimen obtained in office; no leukocytes, no nitrites, no bacteria seen on microscopy. Urine culture not indicated at this time given negative microscopy.

Assessment: Mixed urinary symptoms with urgency, urge incontinence, and possible incomplete emptying in the setting of a cystocele. Given the combination of storage and possible voiding-phase complaints, plan to proceed with urodynamic evaluation (uroflowmetry, cystometrogram, and pressure-flow study) to clarify the underlying etiology — detrusor overactivity versus outlet obstruction from prolapse versus impaired contractility — before deciding on further management, which may include pessary fitting, medication adjustment, or surgical referral. Testing will be limited to the studies needed to answer this specific clinical question; no additional ancillary tests are planned at this time.

Plan: Schedule multichannel urodynamics with fluoroscopy as above. Continue to monitor for signs of infection; none currently present. Follow up after testing to discuss results and next steps.
